source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: ERP vendor master record (including bank details)
ERP vendor master bank account configuration
Scheduled payment to vendor bank account

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The only safeguard against a fraudulent bank-detail change is a human approval step driven entirely by a model-written one-line summary; the prompt gives no structural, out-of-band verification instruction before trusting invoice-stated bank details.
No limit is stated on invoice amount, vendor scope, or payment frequency; the agent matches and pays 'each invoice' with no declared ceiling.

elements.name: Supplier submitting invoices via the portal
Supplier invoice upload into the agent
Payment instruction to vendor bank account
ERP vendor master record (including bank details)

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only a one-line model-written summary, not the bank account number or change history, so a more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary can win approval (ASI09); the gate is further diluted by approval volume of roughly 150 cards/day.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of new vendor bank details
controls.decay_rationale: If the verification contact is pulled from the existing vendor record rather than the invoice, and enforced outside the model, this does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Raw-action approval review for bank and payment changes
controls.decay_rationale: Once the approver sees the actual destination account and a diff against the system of record instead of a model summary, a more capable model cannot write around it.

controls.name: Per-transaction and daily spend cap on scheduled payments
Tamper-evident attributable audit log for bank and payment actions
Least-privilege ERP credential scoped to matched vendor

findings.title: Untrusted invoice drives bank-detail change and payment through a summary-gated, high-volume approval (TC9-style)

attack_path.note: A supplier-portal invoice claims new bank details for a known vendor; the upload's authenticity is not independently verified.
Agent updates the vendor master's bank account from invoice content alone, using a broad ERP credential that can update any vendor.
Agent schedules payment on the due date to the now-fraudulent bank account.

forecast.watch_signal: Model/version string changes without a new review; the approval gate is removed, narrowed to batch/remembered approval, or autonomy is raised beyond A2; daily approvals per clerk remain well above roughly 20.

evidence.observation: Instruction: 'If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record,' meaning content from the untrusted supplier invoice directly drives erp.update_vendor_bank_details with no independent verification step.

The card shown to the clerk displays only a one-line summary ('Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)') with no bank account number or change history, so the approver cannot verify the destination account before approving.

"Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown" to the clerk, and "The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment," so a single spoofed or compromised invoice can redirect payment for any vendor the agent has access to.

recommendations.action: Require independent, out-of-band verification (e.g., a phone call to a known-good number already on file, not one supplied in the invoice) before executing erp.update_vendor_bank_details.

Change the clerk approval card to raw-action review: show the full new bank account number (or a verifiable hash/last-4 plus a diff against the prior value) and the change history, instead of a one-line model-generated summary.
Scope the ERP credential used by the agent to least privilege (vendors on open POs only) rather than organization-wide vendor update and payment authority.

findings.title: No spend or rate limit on scheduled payments (denial-of-wallet / runaway payment exposure)

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed, disabled, or granted as a standing 'always allow' rather than per-request review; autonomy level raised beyond A2.

evidence.observation: The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day and no per-transaction or daily spend cap on erp.schedule_payment is described, so high-volume approval is the only limit on total payment volume.
'Schedule payment on the due date' contains no amount, frequency, or aggregate limit.

recommendations.action: Add a per-transaction and daily aggregate spend cap on erp.schedule_payment enforced outside the model.

Reduce per-approver daily volume for payment and bank-change requests (route to multiple reviewers or throttle submissions) so each request gets individual scrutiny instead of high-volume rubber-stamping.

findings.title: No attributable, tamper-evident record of agent-initiated bank changes and payments

forecast.watch_signal: Vendor scope or payment types are expanded without first adding attributable, tamper-evident logging that distinguishes agent-initiated actions from human decisions.

evidence.observation: "Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown" implies some change history may exist but is not confirmed to be tamper-evident, attributable to agent vs. human action, or used in review; no audit control is described in any artifact.

recommendations.action: Record a tamper-evident, attributable log entry for every bank-detail change and payment, distinguishing agent-initiated steps from the human approver's decision, and surface it during review.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates to the ERP system or whether its identity or session could be spoofed by another process or service account.

No capability lets the agent modify its own configuration or prompt (can_modify_own_config is false); invoice-driven tampering with business data is captured under store.vendor_master, not agent self-tampering.
The approval summary already omits bank account numbers, and no other output channel is described that would disclose vendor or payment data outside the organization.
Supplier-side non-repudiation of invoice submission is outside this agent's control boundary and is not a property the agent design can enforce.
This is an inbound ingestion flow from the supplier portal into the agent; it does not carry internal data outward, so there is no confidentiality exposure on this flow.
The artifacts do not describe any rate limit or volume cap on invoice uploads, so there is not enough information to assess flooding or cost-harvesting risk on this ingestion flow.
Sharing vendor identity and payment amount with the banking network is required for payment execution and is not an excess disclosure beyond normal function.
The artifacts do not state who else can query erp.read_vendor or whether read access to bank details is restricted beyond this agent, so broader exposure cannot be assessed.
No design detail suggests write volume to the vendor master could exhaust ERP resources independent of the payment spend cap already assessed on flow.payment_execution.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted supplier invoice can directly drive an irreversible bank-detail change (configure) and an irreversible payment (spend) via a broad, unscoped ERP credential (rubric U x S3). The only control, the clerk approval card, lowers residual to high: it is structural but partially dependent (model-summary review, ASI09) and operates at high volume (~150/day), so rubric section 5 step 2 credits it only one tier, and the approval-gate floor keeps residual from falling below moderate regardless of other recommendations. Two property gaps compound the exposure: no spend or step limit on scheduled payments (denial-of-wallet; high inherent, moderate residual through the same approval credit), and no attributable, tamper-evident record of agent- versus human-initiated actions (repudiation; high inherent and residual, since no control currently restores it). Under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal, the summary-gated approval fails outright -- a more capable model writes more persuasive summaries, or the gate is removed or narrowed -- returning the primary finding to critical. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.clerk_approval.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md, the approval card, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest, ERP API schema, or IaC was provided; capability scope, exact credential scope, and field-level permissions are inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on some fields (e.g., data_sensitivity, is_egress) is medium.

autonomy.max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not stated and are recorded as null; this is a documentation gap rather than a confirmed unbounded design, and is treated as such wherever it affects the autonomy modifier.

Whether the supplier portal authenticates uploading suppliers, and whether any vendor-record change history is tamper-evident or attributable, is not stated in the artifacts; both are recorded as findings/gaps rather than verified facts.
